title: NIST lists no standard atomic weight for Flerovium (Fl, Z=114)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Flerovium (Fl, Z=114) as blank, with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 114, symbol Fl, as Flerovium. The standard-atomic-weight field for Flerovium is blank in the NIST compositions file. NIST's column note says that for atomic numbers 95 or greater the mass number of the most stable isotope is not specified, because the list of studied isotopes is still incomplete. The relative atomic masses below are the nuclide rows the file does print. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. At least one relative atomic mass on these rows carries a # mark. NIST says a # mark means the value and error were derived not from purely experimental data, but at least partly from systematic trends. Isotope rows in the same file: Fl-289 relative atomic mass 289.19042(60#), isotopic composition blank. A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
